_meta.description: Bundled offline drug-drug interaction + drug-allergy reference for Doc-mate clinical safety surfacing. Well-known pairs only; demo/reference use. NOT a substitute for a maintained clinical database. Severities: contraindicated | major | moderate | minor.

interactions.description: Additive bleeding risk; combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effect increases risk of haemorrhage.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and can potentiate anticoagulation with warfarin.
Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism, raising INR and bleeding risk.
Ciprofloxacin can potentiate warfarin, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
Fluconazole inhibits warfarin metabolism, markedly raising INR.
Metronidazole potentiates warfarin effect, increasing bleeding risk.
Complex interaction altering levels of both drugs; INR and phenytoin levels can shift.
Risk of contrast-associated acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis; metformin is typically held around contrast administration.
Combined potassium retention raises risk of hyperkalaemia.
Additive potassium load raises risk of hyperkalaemia.
Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalaemia, hypotension and renal impairment.
ACE inhibitors can reduce lithium clearance, raising lithium levels.
Additive potassium retention raises risk of hyperkalaemia.
Clarithromycin strongly inhibits simvastatin metabolism, sharply raising risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Amiodarone raises simvastatin exposure, increasing myopathy risk.
Clarithromycin raises atorvastatin exposure, increasing myopathy risk.
Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels; dose limits apply to reduce myopathy risk.
Omeprazole may reduce activation of clopidogrel, potentially lowering antiplatelet effect.
Amiodarone raises digoxin levels, increasing risk of digoxin toxicity.
Verapamil raises digoxin levels and slows conduction, increasing toxicity risk.
Diuretic-induced hypokalaemia potentiates digoxin toxicity.
Additive antifolate effect increases risk of marrow suppression.
NSAIDs reduce methotrexate clearance, raising toxicity risk.
Increased risk of methotrexate toxicity with concurrent use.
Additive serotonergic effect increases risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
High risk of serotonin syndrome; combination is contraindicated.
Linezolid has MAOI activity; combination risks serotonin syndrome.
Additive vasodilation can cause profound, potentially fatal hypotension.
Additive QT prolongation increases risk of serious arrhythmia.
Ciprofloxacin markedly raises tizanidine levels, risking severe hypotension and sedation.
Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels, risking toxicity and seizures.
Additive negative chronotropic/inotropic effect risks bradycardia and heart block.
Additive AV nodal suppression risks bradycardia and heart block.
NSAIDs reduce lithium clearance, raising lithium levels and toxicity risk.
Thiazides reduce lithium clearance, raising lithium levels.
Allopurinol blocks azathioprine metabolism, sharply increasing marrow-suppression risk.
Rifampicin induces metabolism of contraceptives, reducing efficacy.
Beta-blockers can mask warning signs of hypoglycaemia.
Ibuprofen can blunt the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of aspirin.
Dual antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk (may be intentional; verify indication).
Additive oto- and nephrotoxicity with concurrent use.
